title: A2A — Agent-to-Agent Protocol
service: agentcard: the lesson's writer agent serving tasks/send and follow-up messages, a caller that downloads its report in base64 chunks, a SQLite task store, signed Agent Card discovery and skill choice, a length-prefixed frame binding for streamed tasks, and caller views of a multi-hop delegation

parts.lesson_anchor: Task lifecycle (submitted -> working -> input_required -> working -> completed, terminal states, rejected); Messages and Parts; Artifacts (streamed as chunks, the caller accumulates); code/main.py writer_tasks_send, writer_tasks_reply, finish
planted_bugs: target_length reads only the first data part; the first message has its targetLength in the middle of three, so the task waits in input_required, and the AttributeError surfaces two calls away, in artifact_chunks under read_report
tasks_send never looks at the card, so an unknown skill goes working and completed instead of submitted -> rejected
tasks_reply ignores terminal states: a reply to a completed task reopens it, finishes it again and replaces its artifact
ArtifactAssembler.add concatenates, slices, validates and decodes all the base64 received so far on every chunk, quadratic over 20000 chunks
parts.timing_assert: 20000 chunks of 9 base64 characters (135000 bytes) under 0.12 s; the starter takes 1.22 to 1.51 s unloaded and up to 3.6 s under load, the reference 3.7 to 5.4 ms; the natural bytes += fix takes 31 to 45 ms
parts.overfix_guard: chunk boundaries fall inside 4-character groups (7 characters per chunk for the report, 9 for the timing), so decoding each chunk on its own, with or without added padding, fails; received must grow chunk by chunk and a bad group must fail once it is complete, which rules out decoding everything in finish(); targetLength sits in the middle data part, which rules out data[-1]; a reply to a rejected task must also raise, which rules out checking only completed; the terminal check must come before the reply is recorded; a group in base64url's alphabet must raise, which rules out decoding without validate=True

deviations: Part 1: the four suggested defects are kept. The first failure surfaces in the caller's download (read_report into artifact_chunks), two calls from the data-part bug. The writer returns its report as a file part (report.md), so the artifact travels as base64 cut every N characters, as the suggested overfix guard needs. The suggested 20000 chunks are kept (9 characters each); the limit is 0.12 s, which leaves 10x below the starter's fastest run and 22x above the reference's slowest, and lets the still-quadratic bytes += and keep-the-whole-text fixes pass with about 2x to spare.

Part 2: as suggested, plus two rules the round trip needs: load returns the task as it was saved rather than the live object, and a second save replaces the first in one transaction. task_ids is sorted by id instead of insertion order, and the UTF-8 decode and missing-commit traps are not featured, because earlier lessons of this chapter already use them twice (the round trip still catches them).

Part 3: as suggested. The signature field follows the lesson's quiz Q11 (HS256, kid, base64url without padding over canonical JSON with ensure_ascii=False). discover() and delegate() are given glue, so the work is check_card, canonical_json, sign_card, verify_card and choose_skill. outputModes are the lesson card's text and artifact.

Part 4: frames carry status events and numbered text pieces (seq per artifact), and the writer is an async generator over a fake model, with probes on when the working status and the first piece go out. A model error ends the stream with a final failed status, and a caller that closes the stream cancels the task and must close the model's stream. The suggested characters-versus-bytes length trap is not featured, because 03 and 11 already use it: the writer's JSON uses json.dumps defaults, so the trap only bites a candidate who switches to ensure_ascii=False, and the reader is still fed raw UTF-8 frames cut at every byte. The part adds a MAX_FRAME limit checked from the header alone, per-artifact seq checks and nothing after the final status.

Part 5: as suggested, with two rules that make opacity concrete: an artifact reaches a caller only when every hop on the way forwards it, and each delegate is required (the default) or optional for its caller, so the caller's own state follows its own rule. The client's delegation is hop 1. No cycles.
